stories.headline: Tensions Rise in Middle East as US and Iran Trade Threats and Strait of Hormuz Shipping Drops
stories.body:
Tensions between the United States and Iran escalated sharply after military moves, harsh statements, and a reduction in maritime traffic in the Middle East. US President Donald Trump stated on August 18, 2026, that the United States has no talks planned with Iran. On social media, President Trump posted a map depicting the Strait of Hormuz as US territory. In response, Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei mocked President Trump's claims of controlling the critical waterway on August 18, 2026.

Naval security in the area remains highly unstable. Crossings through the Strait of Hormuz fell 19.5% to 95 transits last week, according to data from shipping platform Kpler. An unidentified projectile struck and damaged the engine room of a vessel near Oman in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a casualty among the crew. Iranian negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that the Strait of Hormuz will remain shut until the United States lifts its port blockade and oil sanctions, releases frozen assets, and ends all military operations.

Military actions and threats have expanded across the region. The United Arab Emirates Defence Ministry reported that its air defence systems detected two Iranian ballistic missiles, both of which fell harmlessly into the sea. Meanwhile, Major General Amir Hatami, who commands Iran's Artesh army, announced a $30,000 reward for the killing or capture of any US soldier. Unrelated military activity was also reported in Syria, where eight air strikes hit the Abu al-Duhur military base in the eastern countryside of Idlib, causing physical damage but no reported casualties.

Inside Iran, political tensions and domestic crackdowns continue alongside the international standoff. Mahmood Amiry-Moghaddam, the founder of Iran Human Rights, reported that Iran has executed 28 political prisoners so far in 2026.

stories.headline: UK Reaffirms Support for Ukraine Amid Strikes on Power Plants and Infrastructure
stories.body:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated on August 18, 2026, that the United Kingdom will continue to support Ukraine 100%. The pledge comes as fighting causes civilian casualties and damage to power infrastructure.

A Russian strike damaged equipment at a thermal power plant operated by DTEK in central Ukraine, forcing the facility to halt operations. Russian missile strikes on the village of Pechenihy in northeastern Ukraine killed 10 civilians. Furthermore, a drone strike near the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant killed one nuclear specialist and wounded 17 people. The International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed that the strike hit nuclear staff at a bus stop. Meanwhile, Russian officials stated that Ukrainian forces launched around 620 drones towards the Moscow region overnight.

Diplomatic and internal political developments continue in Kyiv. Former Ukrainian defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov released a video address on August 18, 2026, calling for a wartime presidential election. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy formally nominated acting defence minister Yevhen Khmara to permanently assume the position. On the same day, German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider arrived in Kyiv to discuss resilient infrastructure renewal.

stories.headline: US Imposes Sanctions on International Criminal Court Officials
stories.body:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced new sanctions targeting International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane and Senior Trial Lawyer Abdoulaye Seye. The sanctions freeze their assets in the United States and restrict US entities from engaging in financial transactions with them starting September 17. To facilitate a transition, the US Treasury Department issued a general licence permitting the wind-down of transactions involving Akane through September 17.

The court previously drew US anger when it issued arrest warrants in 2024 for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Israeli Defence Minister Yoav Gallant.

The measures face legal challenges inside the United States. Four US human rights groups filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration in a New York court, alleging that its campaign to dismantle the ICC violates the US Constitution. That lawsuit follows an earlier case filed in June in a New York federal court by three ICC judges—Kimberly Prost, Solomy Balungi Bossa, and Reine Alapini-Gansou—who sued the US administration over its actions.

stories.headline: States Sue Meta in California Federal Court Over Alleged App Addiction in Children
stories.body:
Opening statements began on August 18, 2026, in a federal court in California in a massive lawsuit brought against Meta by a coalition of 29 US states. California Deputy Attorney General Megan O'Neill told the court that Meta deliberately designed its products to hook users, harvest their data, and hide the truth from the public.

The coalition of states is seeking financial penalties of approximately $200 billion from the social media giant. Meta previously faced legal trouble over similar issues and was ordered to pay $942 million in fines in a separate lawsuit in New Mexico.

High-profile witnesses are slated to take the stand during the proceedings in California. Meta Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg and former Meta employee Arturo Bejar are both expected to testify as the landmark trial unfolds.

stories.headline: South Korea Reassesses Alliance After Trump Orders Cut in Military Drills
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump ordered a substantial reduction in joint military exercises with South Korea just before the start of the scheduled Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises. The joint drills were originally scheduled to involve approximately 18,000 South Korean troops alongside US forces. The United States currently maintains about 28,500 troops stationed in South Korea.

In response to the sudden policy change, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung stated on August 18, 2026, that a firm military alliance with the United States continues to underpin South Korea's national security.

However, President Lee also renewed calls for South Korea to gain greater military independence. He urged accelerated efforts to transfer wartime operational control of South Korean forces from the United States back to South Korea. In addition, President Lee called for faster progress on South Korea's nuclear-powered submarine program.

stories.headline: Supreme Court and Education Ministry Intervene Following Mass Student Protests
stories.body:
The Supreme Court of India and the Union Education Ministry have stepped in following mass student protests over competitive examinations.

Delhi Police submitted a 42-page affidavit to the Supreme Court late on August 17, 2026, detailing a major demonstration on July 20. Police reported that over 30,000 protesters were met by 5,000 uniformed officers on that day. Conflicting reports emerged regarding injuries. Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju claimed that no protester was seriously injured or suffered broken bones. However, a Right to Information response revealed that 10 people were wounded by pellets during the protest march.

Politicians are now demanding relief for students. Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Saurav Das issued a two-day ultimatum to the Union government to honor commitments to withdraw police cases (FIRs) against protesters. The Supreme Court requested Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to provide details of FIRs against student protesters so the court can consider quashing them under Article 142.

Meanwhile, ministry leadership has changed after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25, 2026, and Pralhad Joshi took over. Joshi directed a four-tier question paper checking system and new security infrastructure at the National Testing Agency, which also removed 600 experts in an team overhaul.

stories.headline: Former Delhi Minister Satyendar Jain Arrested in Jal Board Corruption Case
stories.body:
The Anti-Corruption Branch of the Delhi government has arrested former Delhi minister and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Satyendar Jain in connection with alleged corruption involving the Delhi Jal Board tendering process.

Investigating officials arrested five other individuals alongside Satyendar Jain. Those taken into custody include former Delhi Jal Board Chief Executive Officer Udit Prakash Rai and former consultant Ankit Srivastava. According to allegations made by Anti-Corruption Branch investigators, Udit Prakash Rai received ₹1.52 crore through a firm named AN Enterprises to purchase immovable property.

Leaders of the Aam Aadmi Party strongly denied all charges and condemned the arrests. AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal asserted that the corruption charges against Satyendar Jain were completely fake and manufactured at the behest of the rival Bharatiya Janata Party. Senior AAP leader Manish Sisodia also criticized the action, explicitly linking Satyendar Jain's arrest to political maneuvering ahead of upcoming assembly elections in Punjab.

stories.headline: Goa Government Seeks Life Imprisonment for Tarun Tejpal in Supreme Court Appeal
stories.body:
The Goa government has filed an appeal in the Supreme Court of India seeking to increase the sentence of former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal to life imprisonment.

Tarun Tejpal was originally acquitted by a Goa trial court in May 2021 in a 2013 rape case. However, the Bombay High Court set aside that acquittal on August 6, 2026, finding him guilty and sentencing him to 10 years of imprisonment.

In its new petition to the Supreme Court, the Goa government is challenging the High Court's ruling that allowed Tarun Tejpal's two aggravated rape sentences to run concurrently rather than consecutively. The state is asking the top court to enhance the penalty to a life sentence.

stories.headline: Audit Shows Most of PM CARES Fund Corpus Held in Fixed Bank Deposits
stories.body:
Newly published financial accounts show that the vast majority of the PM CARES Fund is held in bank fixed deposits while spending remains extremely low.

Audited financial statements for FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25 were signed by auditors on August 7, 2026, and officially published on August 17. By the end of FY 2024-25, the closing balance of the fund reached ₹8,452.06 crore. Audited accounts reveal that ₹7,846 crore of that total corpus was held in fixed deposits with scheduled banks.

Donations to the fund dropped by 30% compared to the previous year, with PM CARES receiving ₹480 crore in FY 2024-25. The fund also received ₹324.66 crore in refunds from implementing agencies during the same financial year. Despite the massive balance, PM CARES spent just ₹87.85 lakh in FY 2024-25, which amounted to 0.01% of its available closing balance.
